title: LibRPA segfault (app_rpa.cpp:115) because librpa.in is not staged in the per-iteration directory
symptom: LibRPA segfaults at driver/app_rpa.cpp:115 during cOpt basis-optimization iterations that run ABACUS and LibRPA in per-iteration directories; the Slurm logs also show 'module: command not found' and the suspicion that ABACUS had not finished before LibRPA started. Fixing libstdc++ did not remove the segfault.
root_cause: cp_files_rpa in cOpt/object/cal_exe.py copies ORBITAL_RESULTS, INPUT, KPT, STRU, pp and CHG into the iteration directory but NOT librpa.in, so LibRPA is launched with no input file to read and crashes in its reader rather than reporting a clean missing-input error.
minimal_fix: Patch cp_files_rpa to also copy librpa.in from abacus_inputs when it exists, with a fallback lookup at abacus_inputs/../librpa.in or the chg staging location. Independently, enforce a real producer->consumer dependency (--dependency=afterok:<abacus_job_id>, or an explicit guard that aborts unless OUT.ABACUS/running_scf.log shows normal completion and every required LibRPA input exists) and source the module environment explicitly in the batch script (or use absolute paths).
validation: After the patch every iteration directory must contain librpa.in next to the copied INPUT/KPT/STRU/pp/CHG, the Slurm log must show no 'module: command not found', the ABACUS log must finish before LibRPA starts, and app_rpa.cpp:115 must no longer segfault so LibRPA*.out completes.
avoid: Do not treat the crash as purely a LibRPA code bug or a stale binary, do not rerun the same iteration hoping LibRPA picks its input up from a parent directory, do not treat it as an ABACUS or basis-set defect, and do not launch LibRPA from the same script line as ABACUS without a dependency or completion guard.

parameters.librpa.in: must be staged in every LibRPA working directory (copy from abacus_inputs, fallback abacus_inputs/../librpa.in)
parameters.module_env: source the module system explicitly in the Slurm batch script
